licenses.text:
Fyodor Dostoevsky, Crime and Punishment, translated by Constance Garnett.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/fyodor-dostoevsky/crime-and-punishment/constance-garnett

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Fyodor Dostoevsky, the author, died 1881 (UK for the text used (1914 English translation first published in London by the British translator); original Russian 1866).
- Constance Garnett, the translator, died 1946.

First publication of the text used: 1914 (SE colophon: 'Crime and Punishment was published in 1866 by Fyodor Dostoevsky. It was translated from Russian in 1914 by Constance Garnett').

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1914, before 1931;
  a published work enters the United States public domain 95 years after
  publication, so this work entered it in 2009.
- Country of origin (UK for the text used (1914 English translation first published in London by the British translator); original Russian 1866): copyright there lasts for life plus 70 years
  after the death of the last surviving person named above. The last to die
  did so in 1946, so the work entered the public domain there on
  1 January 2017.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- Given repo slug does not exist; the actual SE repo is fyodor-dostoevsky_crime-and-punishment_constance-garnett and its colophon was used
- SE colophon: original 1866, Garnett translation 1914; no editor/introducer mentioned
- Wikidata Q991 (Fyodor Dostoyevsky, 'Russian novelist 1821-1881'), P570 = 1881-02-09
- Garnett death year 1946 verified as for the Chekhov repo (Wikidata Q2495818 + English Wikipedia lead + Oxford DNB)
